title: AI Prompt Guard
description:
Enterprise only. Declares once, at the service level, the custom guards that inspect the request body and block prompt injection, jailbreaks, and other malicious content. Endpoints and backends select these guards by `name`, together with the default guards that KrakenD ships.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/ai-gateway/prompt-guard/

guards.title: Guards
guards.description:
The list of custom guards available to endpoints and backends. Each guard has a unique `name`, a `kind` that defines how it evaluates the request, a `severity`, and a `config` whose fields depend on the `kind`.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/ai-gateway/prompt-guard/

config.title: Guard Configuration
config.description:
The settings of the guard. Its fields depend on the `kind`: `patterns` for a `regex` guard, `url` and `score_threshold` for a `classifier` guard, and `expressions` for a `policy` guard.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/ai-gateway/prompt-guard/

kind.title: Guard Kind
kind.description:
How the guard evaluates the request. A `regex` guard matches the body against a list of regular expressions, a `classifier` guard sends the body to an external service that returns a score, and a `policy` guard evaluates CEL expressions against the body and the request metadata.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/ai-gateway/prompt-guard/

name.title: Guard Name
name.description:
A unique name for this guard. Endpoints and backends reference the guard through this value in their `guards` list.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/ai-gateway/prompt-guard/

severity.title: Severity
severity.description:
The severity level assigned to the guard, from `critical` (highest) to `low` (lowest). Endpoints and backends can disable all the default guards of a given severity by adding `!critical`, `!high`, `!medium`, or `!low` to their `guards` list.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/ai-gateway/prompt-guard/

classifier_config.title: Classifier Guard Configuration
classifier_config.description:
The settings of a `classifier` guard, which delegates the decision to an external service. KrakenD sends the request body to the `url`, and the service responds with a JSON object containing a `score` between `0.0` and `1.0`.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/ai-gateway/prompt-guard/

on_failure_block.title: Block on Failure
on_failure_block.description:
Decides what happens when the external classifier cannot be reached or returns an error. Set it to `true` to block the request, or to `false` to let it through.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/ai-gateway/prompt-guard/

score_threshold.title: Score Threshold
score_threshold.description:
The score that decides whether the request passes. The guard blocks the request when the score returned by the external classifier is below this value.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/ai-gateway/prompt-guard/

url.title: Classifier URL
url.description:
The full URL of the external classifier service that receives the request body.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/ai-gateway/prompt-guard/

policy_config.title: Policy Guard Configuration
policy_config.description:
The settings of a `policy` guard, which evaluates CEL expressions against the request.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/ai-gateway/prompt-guard/

expressions.title: Expressions
expressions.description:
The list of CEL expressions to evaluate. Each expression returns a boolean that decides whether the request can continue. Use `body` to inspect the raw payload as a string, and `meta` to access the request `headers`, `params`, `method`, `path`, `query`, and `url`.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/ai-gateway/prompt-guard/

regex_config.title: Regex Guard Configuration
regex_config.description:
The settings of a `regex` guard, which matches the request body against a list of regular expressions.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/ai-gateway/prompt-guard/

patterns.title: Patterns
patterns.description:
The list of regular expressions to match against the request body. The guard blocks the request when any pattern matches. KrakenD merges the patterns of all regex guards, including the default ones, into a single set that it evaluates in one pass.

See: https://www.krakend.io/docs/enterprise/ai-gateway/prompt-guard/
